summary:
Checker of the lane "runtime". Skills used: ariakit-general-workflow, web-perf. I wrote nothing in the repository (git status is the same as at the start). All files are in /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/perf/runtime/check/.

What I did (Chrome through Playwright, headless, viewport 1440 by 900; load average 12 to 190 during the work, given beside each set):
- I copied the snapshot of the research lane and ran my own servers: dev 4341, production 4342. I built five production variants from source (4343 to 4347), a dev copy without StrictMode (4348), and a production copy of the real app (4349). All nine servers are stopped. The shared server at 4320 got 3 light requests and still answers 200.
- I ran the key measurements again from the scripts of the research lane, and I added 8 scripts of my own.

Result in one paragraph: the main answer of the report is correct and I confirmed it with a different experiment: the size of the CSS is not the cause. The development mode cause and the frame cause are also correct. But the part about the primitives has errors: the owner file is wrong, the list of "21 rules" is not complete, the proposed workaround does not work, one statement about the real app is false, and the gain of the glider fix is much larger than the report says. I measured the fixes as real source builds, which the report did not do.

Key numbers, review page, scenario "large" (41 rows, 1,740 elements), median of 5 interleaved runs, load average 14 to 27 (measured):
- Key press to next frame, dev against production: S 194 against 58 ms, ArrowDown 141 against 88 ms, A 221 against 101 ms. The report has 195/55, 202/84, 203/101. Reproduced.
- ArrowDown in production, by source build: base 87.9 ms, 21 rule classes removed 40.7 ms, list glider removed 36.7 ms, both 32.4 ms. Style plus layout: 92, 41, 9, 8 ms.
- Scroll of the list, 10 wheel steps, style plus layout: base 848 ms (12,600 elements), rules removed 355 ms, glider removed 57 ms, both 54 ms.
- Dev without StrictMode: ArrowDown 115 ms (141 with), A 138 ms (221 with).
- Cold cost of the sheet in one document: 507 KB sheet 4.6 ms parse and 110 ms first style and layout; 189 KB sheet (only the 766 rules that can match) 1.9 ms and 111 ms.
verdict:
Confirmed with corrections. Three of the conclusions hold after an attempt to refute each one: (1) the size of the generated CSS is not the cause (measured again, and measured cold, which the report did not do); (2) development mode multiplies the script time of each interaction (reproduced: script 3.8 to 5.7 times, next frame 1.6 to 3.4 times); (3) the live frames are a lab-only cost (counts reproduced: 4,857 to 4,893 requests for the gallery in dev, 1,365 in production).

Not confirmed as written: the two causes in the primitives. The effect is real and I reproduced it (largest layout 60.5 ms with all rules, 11.9 ms without the 21). But the report names the wrong owner (@ariakit/tailwind; the variants are in src/components/ariakit/styles/ui.css and the recipe files), gives a shape that is too narrow, proposes a workaround that I measured as no gain, says that the real app has no glider (it has one), and gives estimates for the fixes that are 2 times too pessimistic. Its production load numbers come from a copy with a broken style link (effect 5 to 7%).

corrections.claim: Fix for the 21 rules: "In @ariakit/tailwind: do not generate a selector that has :has() on an ancestor with a * subject".
corrections.problem: Wrong owner (documented, read in source). The variants are not in @ariakit/tailwind. They are `@custom-variant` blocks in the copied file apps/lab/src/components/ariakit/styles/ui.css: `ui-disabled-within` (line 976), `ui-field-disabled` (990), `ui-choice-on` (1141), `ui-choice-disabled` (1174). That file only has `@import "@ariakit/tailwind"` at line 1. The recipes join them with Tailwind core variants (`**:`, `*:`, `group-…/name:`, `not-…:`), and Tailwind core writes the wrapper `:is(… *)`. Source lines: choice.ts 45, 51, 52, 108, 134, 195, 284; control.ts 366, 371; input.ts 32.
corrections.fix: Name the owner as the Ariakit UI style layer (ui.css and the recipes in src/components/ariakit/styles), with Tailwind core as the source of the `:is(… *)` wrapper. Example of a class to rewrite: `group-ui-disabled-within/choice:ak-ink-0` compiles to `.x:is(:is(:where(.group\/choice):is(:disabled,…), :where(.group\/choice):has(:is(:disabled,…))) *)`.

corrections.claim: The cause is "21 rules that have :has() on an ancestor and a * subject".
corrections.problem: The shape is wider and the list is not complete (measured). In 12 of the 21 the subject is a class, not `*`. One synthetic rule that no element matches gives the full cost: `.zz-never:has(.qq-never) * {}` gives 58 ms largest layout and 1,704 recalculated elements for each press, against 11.9 ms and 607 without (3 rounds, load 90 to 150). The same for `> *`, and for the shape inside `:is()` and `:not()`. A class subject after `:has()` is fast (12.6 ms, 631 elements). And in the build without the 21 rules and without the list glider, the view with all folders open still recalculates 2,432 of 2,594 elements for each press, with the reason "Affected by :has()" and a subtree invalidation of BODY.
corrections.fix: State the rule as a shape, not as a list: no selector in the built sheet may have a `:has()` compound followed by a combinator and `*`. Check it in the built CSS and with the trace category `disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline.invalidationTracking` (script: check/invalidation.mjs). My count of the shape: 23 rules in the lab sheet, 8 in the real app sheet, 3 left in the build without the 21.

corrections.problem: It does not work (measured, source build, 5 interleaved runs, load 91 to 172). ArrowDown to next frame: 85.9 ms [83.9-88.3] with the workaround, 93.3 ms [90.7-116.1] without. Layout 73.1 against 79.7 ms. Scroll: 13,747 recalculated elements against 12,658. The sheet still has 6 rules of the shape from control.ts and input.ts (counted), and the report says itself that one rule is enough. The workaround also removes the styles of the checkbox and radio recipes (sheet 475,107 to 441,257 bytes).
corrections.fix: Remove the workaround from the answer. The source change that works is in the recipes: with the 10 class names removed from choice.ts, control.ts, and input.ts in a copy, ArrowDown is 40.7 ms [38.1-47.2] against 87.9 ms (load 14 to 27). That was a test of the gain, not a proposal for the look.

corrections.claim: "The list of the real app today has no glider."
corrections.problem: False (documented and measured). apps/web/src/review/item-list.tsx line 307 has `glider={{ $kind: "bar", $state: "selected", $side: "end", $barOffset: "frame" }}`. apps/web/src/components/app-shell.tsx line 49 has the same. The real app page has 5 `.glider` elements. With the gliders hidden by CSS in the real app, an ArrowDown has 0.9 ms of layout against 11.9 ms, and 5.9 ms of recalculation against 11.4 ms (3 rounds, each press).
corrections.fix: Say: the real app has one selected bar glider in its list, and the design has four (hover, selected, focus, bar). The glider is already about 70% of the style and layout time of an ArrowDown in the real app today, but the page is small (705 elements), so the total is 30 ms.

corrections.claim: With the nav glider hidden: ArrowDown 85 to 34 ms (57 in the first run), scroll layout 181 to 11 ms. Estimate for both fixes: 60 to 65 ms to the next frame, 250 to 300 ms at 4 times CPU.
corrections.problem: The report hid the glider with `display: none`, so the glider classes and their `:has()` rules stayed. A real removal of the `glider` prop gives more (measured, source build, load 14 to 27): ArrowDown 87.9 to 36.7 ms to the next frame, style plus layout 92 to 9 ms, scroll style plus layout 848 to 57 ms, recalculated elements in the scroll 12,600 to 1,355. Both fixes together: 32.4 ms, not 60 to 65. At 4 times CPU (load 43 to 77): 450 ms base, 162 ms without the glider, 191 ms without the rules.
corrections.fix: Replace the estimates with these measured values. Also say that the two causes are one mechanism: without the list glider, the 21 rules cost nothing in the 41-row view (36.7 ms against 32.4 ms).

corrections.claim: Production load numbers: bare preview 159 requests, 1.5 to 1.9 s of main-thread work; gallery 1,385 requests.
corrections.problem: The production copy of the research lane served a broken style link (counted and measured). Its server HTML links `/assets/styles-DatjSvDY.css`, which returns 404; the client build wrote `styles-_WVGwkaQ.css`. Its preview log has 772 requests for the missing file. Cause: the copy had no ignore rule for `dist`, so Tailwind scanned the client output when it built the server (475,355 against 475,107 bytes). With a `.gitignore` line `dist/` my rebuild gives one hash for both. Effect on a load: main-thread work 1,685 against 1,609 ms cold and 1,388 against 1,295 ms warm (5 to 7%), 159 against 158 requests, gallery 1,385 against 1,365. Interactions are not affected.
corrections.fix: Add this limit to the report. The repository build does not have the problem: apps/lab/dist has `styles-BS3en6FB.css` in both client and server (counted). So "review the lab from a production build" is safe advice.

corrections.claim: Development mode: "No code change makes development mode as fast as production."
corrections.problem: True, but the report missed one named and removable part (documented and measured). The default client entry of TanStack Start wraps the app in StrictMode: node_modules/@tanstack/react-start/dist/plugin/default-entry/client.tsx. Neither app has its own src/client.tsx. In dev, StrictMode renders each component two times. A copy with a client entry without StrictMode: S 159 against 194 ms, ArrowDown 115 against 141 ms, A 138 against 221 ms; script of ArrowDown 79 against 172 ms (5 runs, load 14 to 27).
corrections.fix: Name StrictMode as 15 to 54% of the dev script of an interaction. Give the option: a `src/client.tsx` without StrictMode for a design session. The cost is the loss of the StrictMode checks. Without it, dev script is still 1.7 to 4.3 times the production script.

corrections.claim: Inside the lab frame the keys cost the same as in the bare preview (difference below 10%).
corrections.problem: True only with no throttling. The report's own table at 4 times CPU in production has S 255 against 225 ms (+13%), A 582 against 464 ms (+25%), ArrowDown 613 against 418 ms (+47%), with wide ranges. I did not measure this again.
corrections.fix: Say "below 10% with no throttling; 13 to 47% more at 4 times CPU in production, with wide ranges".

corrections.claim: Script by owner in development: React 68%, clava 13%, @ariakit/react 12%, design code 2.7%, primitives 1.8%.
corrections.problem: Close, but the number for design code leaves out a forced layout. My profile (39 key presses, load 12 to 17, 4,364 ms of script): React 61.6%, design code 13.2%, clava 11.9%, @ariakit/react 10.4%, primitives 1.4%. Of the design code time, 486 ms is `getBoundingClientRect` called in an effect: screenshot-list.tsx lines 177 and 178 (current source) and use-row-fit.ts lines 40 and 42. That is 12.5 ms for each key press.
corrections.fix: Give both numbers and name the forced layout. It moves the layout into the task of the key press. I did not measure a gain from its removal.

corrections.claim: The glider props are at lines 252 and 305 of src/explorations/kits/ariakit/list/screenshot-list.tsx.
corrections.problem: That is the snapshot of 04:18. In the current source the lines are 246 and 299 (counted).
corrections.fix: Use the current lines, or cite the text `glider={gliders}`.

causes.cause: Live frames in the lab. Each frame is a whole document with its own modules, React tree, and style sheet.
causes.size: Counted, load 30 to 144, 2 runs: gallery (15 frames) 4,857 to 4,893 requests and 24.1 MB in dev cold, 3.1 MB warm; 1,365 requests in production. One bare frame in dev: 417 requests, 20.4 MB (lucide-react 5.7 MB in one file, react-dom 3.1 MB, @ariakit/react 2.2 MB, lab fixtures 62 files, design code 70 files, copied primitives 57 files). Measured: gallery main-thread work about 6.1 s cold and 8.0 s warm in dev, about 5.0 s in production. The report has 9.0 to 11.2 s and 6.0 to 8.6 s at a load of 170 to 850.
causes.fix: Show fewer live frames: a picture first and the live frame on a click, or a smaller margin than `rootMargin: "100% 0px"` in apps/lab/src/lab/ui/preview-frame.tsx. I did not test this fix. A production build alone is not enough for the gallery: it still needs about 5 s of main-thread work.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: No. The real app has no frames. Its run page in production is 13 requests and 264 ms of main-thread work (measured, 5 runs).

causes.cause: React development mode, with StrictMode from the default client entry of TanStack Start (node_modules/@tanstack/react-start/dist/plugin/default-entry/client.tsx). Each interaction runs more script. Style and layout are the same in both modes.
causes.size: Measured, 5 interleaved runs, load 14 to 27. Next frame, dev against production: S 194 against 58 ms, ArrowDown 141 against 88 ms, A 221 against 101 ms. Script: 164 against 33, 172 against 46, 279 against 49 ms (3.8 to 5.7 times). Without StrictMode in dev: S 159, ArrowDown 115, A 138 ms; ArrowDown script 79 ms. At 4 times CPU and load 92 to 189: ArrowDown 1,195 ms in dev against 515 ms in production. Profile: React 61.6% of dev script, of it about 1,300 ms of 4,364 ms in `jsx` and `jsxDEV`.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes. apps/web has the same default entry and no src/client.tsx. The report measured 108 ms in dev against 34 ms in production for ArrowDown there; I measured only production again: 29.7 ms.

causes.cause: The nav glider on the screenshot list (4 gliders: hover, selected, focus, bar). Its rules in src/components/ariakit/styles/nav.ts (`not-ui-nav-glider-selected:hidden`, `[&~.control,&~*_li>.control]:ui-selected:…`) and the variant `ui-nav-glider-selected` in ui.css line 1230 use `:has(~ …)`. They make the Nav root a `:has()` anchor, and the glider moves with anchor positioning in a transition, so each key press has many recalculations and layouts. The hover glider makes each wheel step a hover change.
causes.size: Measured, production source build with the `glider` prop removed from the two Nav elements of the list, 5 interleaved runs, load 14 to 27. ArrowDown next frame 87.9 to 36.7 ms; style plus layout 92 to 9 ms; layouts 13 to 5. A 101 to 55 ms. Scroll of 10 wheel steps: style plus layout 848 to 57 ms, recalculated elements 12,600 to 1,355. At 4 times CPU (load 43 to 77): ArrowDown 450 to 162 ms, scroll 4,136 to 245 ms. With all folders open (585 rows): first hover 281 to 45 ms, scroll 3,606 to 88 ms.
causes.fix: Do not pass `glider` to the Nav of a long list (`glider={gliders}` in src/explorations/kits/ariakit/list/screenshot-list.tsx, lines 246 and 299 of the current source). The selected row keeps its surface: without the glider it paints its own background (measured: `oklch(0.2134 0.0091 264.28)`; pictures in check/shots/). What goes away: the moving highlight, the bar at the end edge, and the hover and focus covers.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes, today. apps/web/src/review/item-list.tsx line 307 has one selected bar glider. Hidden by CSS there, layout for each ArrowDown goes from 11.9 to 0.9 ms. The page is small, so the total is only 30 ms.

causes.cause: A rule shape in the primitive CSS that makes Chrome invalidate the whole subtree of each `:has()` anchor: a `:has()` compound, then a combinator, then `*`, also inside `:is()` or `:not()`. One rule is enough, also when no element matches it. Sources: the `@custom-variant` blocks with `:has()` in src/components/ariakit/styles/ui.css (lines 976, 990, 1141, 1174) joined in the recipes with `**:`, `*:`, `group-…/name:`, and `not-…:` (choice.ts 45, 51, 52, 108, 134, 195, 284; control.ts 366, 371; input.ts 32). No element of the review page has these classes.
causes.size: Measured. Browser experiment, 3 rounds, load 90 to 150: largest layout of an ArrowDown 60.5 ms with all rules, 11.9 ms without the 21, 58 ms with one synthetic rule put back; recalculated elements for each press 1,666, 607, 1,704. Source build without the 10 class names, 5 runs, load 14 to 27: ArrowDown 87.9 to 40.7 ms, A 101 to 55 ms, scroll style plus layout 848 to 355 ms. With the list glider removed, this change adds almost nothing in the 41-row view (36.7 against 32.4 ms).
causes.fix: In the Ariakit UI style layer, write these states without `:has()` before a `*`. Example: `ui-disabled-within:**:ak-ink-0` and `group-ui-disabled-within/choice:ak-ink-0` can read a custom property that the disabled wrapper sets, as `ui-list-last-row` does with `@container style(--list-last-row: 1)`. I did not test a rewrite. Add a check on the built CSS that fails when the shape is present. The workaround `@source not` of the report does not work (85.9 against 93.3 ms).
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes in the sheet: apps/web has 6 `group-ui-disabled-within/` rules of the shape from its control.ts (lines 317, 322, 327). But there, the removal of the rules does not change the count today (207 elements for each press with and without). It will count when the design brings long lists and more gliders.

causes.cause: The screenshot list with all folders open (585 rows, 2,598 elements). A selection change still recalculates the whole document after both fixes above. The trace gives the reason "Affected by :has()" for 258 nodes and 25 subtree invalidations of BODY. The list is also not windowed.
causes.size: Measured, production, 5 runs, load 28 to 73. ArrowDown next frame: 416 to 427 ms base, 358 ms without the glider, 395 ms without the 21 rules, 398 ms with both. With container queries off, the build with both fixes recalculates 2,432 of 2,594 elements for each press (195 to 215 ms).
causes.fix: Not found. The next step is to find which rule makes `body` an anchor (script check/invalidation.mjs gives the invalidation sets). Windowing the list, or `content-visibility: auto` on each row, would lower the count of elements; I did not test either. The default view of a real run has 41 changed rows and 24 closed folders, so this case needs a person to open every folder.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes for the settled design, when it is built into apps/web.

causes.cause: The page of the design is heavier than the page of the real app today: more elements and long class names from the primitives.
causes.size: Measured, production, 5 runs, load 13 to 50. Load of the review page: 1,651 ms of main-thread work cold and 1,403 ms warm (script 735, style 292, layout 515 ms), 158 requests, 90 scripts, 1,740 elements. The run page of the real app with 41 screenshots: 264 ms (script 117, style 50, layout 59 ms), 13 requests, 705 elements. Counted: the server document of the review page is 466,168 bytes (19,629 bytes with gzip), and 64.4% of it is class attributes (1,098 attributes, mean 273 characters, longest 3,314).
causes.fix: Fewer wrapper elements for each row (the report counted 29 elements for a changed row and 5.4 in the real app; I did not count this again). This is design code and primitives together. No fix was tested.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes for the settled design. It is the size of the load cost that the new review page will have.

causes.cause: The size of the generated CSS (475 KB, 3,027 style rules).
causes.size: Measured: not a cause. Cold insert in one document, 7 interleaved runs, load 120 to 130: full sheet (507 KB) 4.6 ms parse and 109.9 ms first style and layout; only the 766 rules that can match (189 KB) 1.9 ms and 110.6 ms; the sheet two times (1,014 KB) 8.5 ms and 123 ms. The shared dev server sends 614,316 bytes against 518,014 bytes from a new dev server of the same source (counted): stale class names from a long session. By the numbers above this costs a few ms for each document (estimate).
causes.fix: None needed for speed in the browser. A restart of the dev server removes the stale 96 KB.
causes.sharedWithRealApp: Yes, the same result is expected: the sheet of the real app has almost the same size. Not measured on apps/web.

causes.size: Measured: load average 12 to 190 on 14 cores during my work (16 to 850 during the research). Example: dev ArrowDown was 233 ms at load 92 to 189 and 141 ms at load 14 to 27. Production numbers moved less: 97 against 88 ms.
causes.fix: Use the ratios and the counts. Repeat the absolute times on a free machine before you quote them.

realApp:
What I checked in apps/web as it is (production build of a copy with 41 screenshots and 6 variants each, port 4349):

- Reproduced (measured, 5 runs, load 13 to 25): ArrowDown 29.7 ms to the next frame [27-32.3], 161 ms at 4 times CPU [110-174]. D 18.6 ms and 94 ms. Scroll of 10 wheel steps: script 51, style 44, layout 8 ms. The report has 34, 159, 19, 89, and 52/44/8. I did not run the dev server of the real app again, so the report's 108 ms in dev is not rechecked.
- The real app is not slow in the way of the lab today, because its page is small (705 elements, 13 requests, 264 ms of main-thread work for a load) and it has no frames.
- It already has the two things that cost time in the design: one glider in its list (item-list.tsx line 307) and 6 rules of the bad shape in its sheet. Today they cost little: the glider is about 17 of 23 ms of style and layout for each ArrowDown.

What follows for the settled design in apps/web, production build, from the lab copy (measured unless noted):

- As it is built now, default view of a large run (41 changed screenshots, 1,740 elements): S 58 ms, ArrowDown 88 ms, A 101 ms. At 4 times CPU: 258 to 306 ms, 450 to 515 ms, 538 to 615 ms. The limit for a good interaction is 200 ms (documented, web.dev). So a slower laptop is over the limit for the main keys. Scroll: 85 to 106 ms of style and layout for each wheel step.
- Without the glider on the list: ArrowDown 37 ms and 162 ms at 4 times CPU, A 55 ms and 260 ms, scroll 6 ms for each wheel step. With the rule shape fixed and the glider kept: 41 ms and 191 ms, scroll 36 ms for each step.
- Load of the page: about 1.4 to 1.65 s of main-thread work, against 0.26 s for the run page today.
- At the size of a real run (626 screenshots): the default view is the case above. With all 24 folders open (585 rows), ArrowDown is about 400 ms and stays there after both fixes; hover and scroll become fast without the glider (281 to 45 ms, 3.6 s to 0.09 s for 10 steps). The 3,832 variants are not in the page at one time (assumption of the report, not rechecked).
- In `pnpm dev`, each of these is 1.6 to 3.4 times slower to the next frame, and StrictMode is a part of that.

So the fear is justified for one thing, and it is not the size of the CSS: the list with gliders together with the `:has()` rule shape of the primitives. Fix these two before the design goes into apps/web, and find the cause of the 400 ms with all folders open.
remainingDoubts: I did not find the rule that makes `body` a `:has()` anchor with all folders open, so I have no fix for the 400 ms ArrowDown at 585 rows. Windowing and `content-visibility` were not tested.

The reason inside Blink is not read from the Chromium source. The evidence is the experiment with synthetic rules and the words of Chrome's own invalidation trace (`allDescendantsMightBeInvalid: true`, `pseudo=has`).
No rewrite of the recipes was tested. The gain comes from a copy where I deleted 10 class names, which changes the look of disabled and checked choice controls. The real fix must keep that look.

In the real app, the removal of the shape rules or of every `:has()` rule in the browser changes the recalculated count by 0 to 5% (207, 208, 196 elements for each press). So I cannot say that the shape costs anything in apps/web today. The source of its 172-element recalculation is not found.

Not rechecked: the theme switch with 15 frames (5,111 ms), the selector statistics (91.3% primitives, 59% never match), the lab chrome interactions (scenario tab, Look menu), the dev server of the real app (108 ms), the count of 29 elements for each row, and the frame overhead at 4 times CPU.
Only Chrome, headless. No Safari, no Firefox, no compositor or GPU measurement. Anchor positioning and `:has()` invalidation can behave differently in other engines.

The copy is the lab of 04:18. The lab source changed after that (about 50 files differ). The review preview document of the shared server has the same size as my copy (462,398 bytes) and the same 11 gliders, and the current build still has 23 rules of the shape, so the result should hold for the current lab. I did not build the current source.
The machine was never free (load 12 to 190). Absolute times are too high by an unknown factor. The gallery load has only 2 runs.
The fix for the frames (fewer live frames, smaller root margin) was not tested by the report or by me.
The StrictMode result has wide ranges in one of two runs (some values near 0 at load 55 to 77). The second run at load 14 to 27 is clean and agrees.
checks:
All commands ran from /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/perf/runtime/check/. Logs: results-chk-*.log. Raw data: results/chk-*.json.

Setup
- `rsync` of the research copy to check/lab; `make-variant.sh <name> <patch>` for lab-base, lab-noglider, lab-sourcenot, lab-norules, lab-both (each `vite build`, 7 to 10 s). Client and server CSS have one hash in each build (475,107 bytes base; 441,257 sourcenot; 462,930 norules).
- Servers: `run-vite.sh lab --port 4341` (dev), `run-vite.sh lab preview --port 4342`, variants on 4343 to 4347, `run-vite.sh lab-nostrict --port 4348` (dev), `run-vite.sh web preview --port 4349`.
- `stop-servers.sh`: stopped 4341 to 4349. `lsof` shows no listener on these ports. `curl http://127.0.0.1:4320/favicon.svg` gives 200. `git status --short` gives ` M pnpm-lock.yaml` and `?? apps/lab/`, as at the start.

Reproduction of the report
- `node interact.mjs --name chk-A-review --conds dev:bare:1,prod:bare:1,dev:bare:4,prod:bare:4 --reps 5` (load 92 to 189): dev S 202, ArrowDown 233, A 176 ms; production 60, 97, 115 ms; 4 times CPU dev 1,151, 1,195, 1,280 ms; production 306, 515, 615 ms. Scroll production: style 469, layout 544 ms, 13,690 elements.
- `node interact.mjs --name chk-quiet --conds dev:bare:1,nostrict:bare:1,base:bare:1,noglider:bare:1,norules:bare:1,both:bare:1 --reps 5` (load 14 to 27): ArrowDown next frame 140.7, 115.4, 87.9, 36.7, 40.7, 32.4 ms. Scroll style plus layout: 910, 858, 848, 57, 355, 54 ms.
- `node interact.mjs --name chk-web --set web --conds webchk:bare:1,webchk:bare:4 --reps 5`: ArrowDown 29.7 and 161.3 ms.
- `node load-all.mjs --servers dev,base --views gallery --reps 2`: 4,857 and 4,893 requests in dev, 1,365 in production, 15 of 15 frames.

Attempts to refute
- CSS size: `node sheet-cold.mjs --server base --reps 7`: full 4.6 ms parse and 109.9 ms; used (766 of 3,027 rules) 1.9 ms and 110.6 ms; double 8.5 ms and 123 ms.
- Rule shape: `node synthetic.mjs --server base --rounds 3`: base 60.5 ms and 1,666 elements; without the 21 rules 11.9 ms and 607; plus `.zz-never:has(.qq-never) *` 58 ms and 1,704; plus `.zz-never:has(.qq-never) .yy-never` 12.6 ms and 631.
